result:
PR #416 is marked ready, but it does not fix #412. The code change works as designed, and the frame rate moved only from 15.1 to 15.5 fps against a predicted gain of at least 2.

**Why the last session stopped:** it ended correctly, waiting on its device runs. All of them have since finished, and that reason is now in NOTES.md.

**Speed test on the Nova, before (A) and after (B), during mission play:**

| | A | B |
|---|---|---|
| fps | 15.1 | 15.5 |
| GPU drains forced by the full descriptor list, per 60 frames | 39 | 0 |
| renderer time spent waiting on the GPU | 22 ms | 0.2 ms |
| GPU time per frame | 40.0 ms | 28.3 ms |
| time between frames | 63–67 ms | 63.5 ms |

- **What worked:** the list of shader descriptor sets used to run out mid-frame and force a full GPU drain. It now grows into extra pools instead, capped at 16 pools; only 1 was ever used. The drains are gone, and the GPU does 12 ms less work per frame.
- **Why fps didn't move:** the time between frames stayed about the same. The renderer's own work grew by about 10 ms (surface updates and texture binding) and it spent more time idle. So something outside the renderer sets the pace. The emulated game CPU was about 97% busy in both runs.
- **In the pause-menu window** B gained 0.7 fps. Two runs of the unchanged build differed by 0.9 fps there, so that gain is noise.
- **The first A run lost its device connection for part of play.** A rerun was used as A; the first run is kept as a replicate and agrees with it.

**Image tests (the three that must not move):** all 99 captures matched exactly between before and after, with no unreadable results. The new code path never ran in these tests. The two sides ran on different devices (Thor before, Nova after). No official `[job.arms]` verdict had been posted when I read them, so this is my own row-by-row comparison.

**Decision:** I kept the change in the PR. It changes no pixels, removes the forced drains, cuts GPU work and has a fixed cap. The PR, the issue and NOTES all say plainly that the fps prediction failed and #412 stays open.

**Next step for #412, written into NOTES:**
1. Profile the emulated-CPU thread over the pause-menu window.
2. Time the surface-update and texture-bind work with the waits excluded, to see whether the extra 10 ms is a hidden wait. Surface updates live in `vk/surface.c`, which PR #396 also changes, so that file waits until #396 is merged.

**Branch state:** master is merged in (25c3b53d82) and preflight passed. The PR's `Files:` line matches the diff. Both predictions were left unchanged: nothing was rebased, so the builds they name are still in the branch history. Results are posted on PR #416 and issue #412.
